message.content: {"answer": "C", "option_text": "Alveolar rupture causing secondary pneumomediastinum and air tracking into the spinal canal.", "reason": "The provided images are axial CT scans (not chest X-rays) showing extensive pneumomediastinum, subcutaneous emphysema, and air within the spinal canal (pneumorrhachis). The clinical history of forceful vomiting is classic for barotrauma leading to alveolar rupture (Macklin effect), where air tracks along bronchovascular sheaths into the mediastinum and subsequently into the epidural space. This mechanism fits Option C better than esophageal perforation (which typically presents with pleural effusion/mediastinitis) or trauma."}
